rows.classification: N/A (discovery/threshold-derivation period, not a holdout test)

comparison.validation_vs_development: Validation's net_expectancy_10bps (+0.338%) is BETTER than development's (-0.040%) -- but validation's own sample is smaller/narrower (43 trades/20 symbols/10 days vs development's 735/35/63) and sits at the minimum acceptable breadth floor.
comparison.replication_vs_development_and_validatio: Replication's net_expectancy_10bps (-0.224%) is WORSE than both development and validation, and its gross_expectancy REVERSES SIGN relative to both (development +0.060%, validation +0.438%, replication -0.124%) on the broadest sample of the three (182 trades/33 symbols/34 days).
comparison.directional_agreement: Replication does NOT agree directionally with validation or development. This is the decisive negative signal.
comparison.economic_edge_after_costs: Development and replication are both net-negative at 10bps; only validation (the narrowest, most boundary-hugging sample) is net-positive. The one period with the LEAST statistical power is the only one supporting the hypothesis.
comparison.concentration: None of the three periods show single-symbol/single-day domination (all top1 shares well under 40%) -- concentration is not what's driving the negative replication result.
comparison.symmetry: Long/short asymmetry is UNSTABLE across periods: development favors short (+0.112% short vs -0.199% long), validation favors long (+0.460% long vs -0.063% short), replication favors neither (both near/below zero, long -0.347%, short +0.0001%). This instability is itself evidence against a robust, structural fade effect -- a real effect should show a more consistent directional signature across independent periods.

conclusion: The body of evidence across THREE independent periods (development warning sign, validation narrow/boundary pass, replication decisive and broad-sample failure with reversed sign) does not collectively support a credible, robust, cost-adjusted edge.
